definition: An attention pattern where each token only attends to a fixed-size local window of nearby tokens, rather than the entire sequence.
details: Sliding window attention reduces the quadratic computational cost of full self-attention, trading some long-range direct interaction for substantial efficiency gains, often combined with other mechanisms to preserve some long-range information flow.
story: Think of an orchestra warming up: no single instrument carries the piece, but together they make the sound. Here is the short version: An attention pattern where each token only attends to a fixed-size local window of nearby tokens, rather than the entire sequence. The part that makes it sing: Sliding window attention reduces the quadratic computational cost of full self-attention, trading some long-range direct interaction for substantial efficiency gains, often combined with other mechanisms to preserve some long-range information flow. The shape of the machine is half the idea. And that shape of the machine — Sliding Window Attention — is what makes everything else possible.
